title: Let's Talk About John DeLorean
summary: Josh and Chuck profile John DeLorean, the American GM executive turned carmaker behind the DMC DeLorean. They cover his Detroit upbringing and engineering career, his success at Pontiac with the GTO (often called the first muscle car), his rise to Chevrolet and GM's upper ranks, and his departure from GM in 1973. They then describe the DeLorean Motor Company, its Belfast factory funded by British government money, the car's production problems, and the FBI cocaine sting that led to his 1984 acquittal, followed by his later life, death, and the car's fame through Back to the Future. The episode closes with a listener mail about brown noise.

segments.title: Opening banter and documentaries
segments.summary: The hosts introduce John DeLorean as a celebrity, weird figure and carmaker, compare him to modern tech founders, and mention two documentaries about him.

segments.title: Early life and GM engineering career
segments.summary: DeLorean is born in Detroit to immigrant parents, gets a technical education, serves in World War Two, and joins Packard and then General Motors. He earns patents for features like the recessed windshield wiper and hidden antennas, and sees a market for youth-oriented cars.

segments.title: The Pontiac GTO
segments.summary: Working with Bunky Knudson at Pontiac, DeLorean puts a Bonneville engine into the Tempest, creating the GTO package in 1964. It is widely considered the first muscle car and is marketed to young people.

segments.title: Rise at GM and personal life
segments.summary: DeLorean becomes Pontiac general manager at age forty, follows the GTO with the Firebird and Grand Prix, and then moves to Chevrolet and the upper floors of GM. The hosts describe his celebrity image, his relationships with Hollywood actresses, and his marriages.

segments.title: Leaving GM
segments.summary: Rumors of kickbacks and expense abuse circulate in the early 1970s. DeLorean leaves GM in April 1973, either by resignation or firing, and portrays it as his own choice while GM stays quiet.

segments.title: DeLorean Motor Company and the gull-wing car
segments.summary: Despite a noncompete, DeLorean starts the DeLorean Motor Company to build a stainless steel, fuel-efficient sports car. Giugiaro designs it, and the hosts discuss its clunky performance, weight, and slow acceleration.

segments.title: Belfast factory and British funding
segments.summary: The British government offers a large package to build the factory in Belfast, an area of high unemployment and sectarian tension. The plant is built with separate entrances for Protestant and Catholic workers, amid protests, and the Lotus-built production version departs from the prototype.

segments.title: Mid-episode break
segments.summary: A short break in the episode.

segments.title: Collapse and the FBI cocaine sting
segments.summary: The company runs through British money, enters receivership after Thatcher's government stops funding it, and DeLorean is recorded in a 1982 FBI cocaine sting. Entrapment is argued and he is acquitted in August 1984. The hosts also cover the Hustler tapes and a separate Detroit theft case.

segments.title: Later life, death and Back to the Future
segments.summary: DeLorean's later marriages, business plans and collector items are covered. He dies of a stroke at 77. The DeLorean's role as the Back to the Future time machine helps rehabilitate his reputation.

segments.title: Listener mail: Chuck's brown noise
segments.summary: A listener writes that her sister's noisy condo was fixed by the brown noise Chuck recommended, and the hosts respond with a call for listener mail.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts thank listeners and close the episode.
